newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money down to 3.05/3.125 pct with repo.
newsitem.headline: German call money down to 3.05/3.125 pct with repo.

text.p: German call money rates slumped to 3.05/3.125 percent on Wednesday from 3.20/3.25 percent on Tuesday after the Bundesbank added 3.1 billion marks to the market in its weekly repo allotment, traders said.
Most of the dealings were reportedly done at 3.10 percent.

Rates on Tuesday had risen well above the three percent securities repurchase rate and the German central bank had been expected to add up to four billion marks to the market to fill the liquidity gap.
Some traders said the market could have absorbed additional funds, saying the absolute minimum was added to the market.
But others said they were satisfied with the repo allotment and that the anticipated monthly reserve average of 40.7 billion marks could be met without much disruption.

The Bundesbank said commercial bank reserves rose to 39.0 billion marks as of Tuesday compared with 36.4 billion marks on Monday, while the monthly average on Wednesday slipped a bit to 40.0 billion marks from 40.1 billion marks on Tuesday.
